podcast.title: British Rave Scene Descendant
podcast.body: Most of the better-known Alternative Dance came from the UK, being a "direct descendant of the British rave and dance and DJ scene of the 1980s." "Most of the better known Alternative Dance we got came from the UK. It's a direct descendant of the British rave and dance and DJ scene of the 1980s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Continuum with Pure Dance Music
podcast.body: Alternative Dance formed a "vast continuum linking Alternative Music proper with pure dance music," blurring the lines between these genres and expanding the possibilities of electronic music in the mainstream. "It was a vast continuum linking Alternative Music proper with pure dance music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Electronic Basis
podcast.body: Alternative Dance is rooted in electronics, heavily utilizing "lots of keyboards and drum machines and loops and samples" to create its distinct sound. "Again, this was based in electronics. Lots of keyboards and drum machines and loops and samples."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Evolution of 80s Technopop
podcast.body: Essentially, Alternative Dance was described as "souped up 80s Technopop," infused with indie rock sensibilities, indie attitudes, and DJ techniques, including "Turntableism." "Basically, Alternative Dance is souped up 80s Technopop, dressed with Indy Rock and Indy Attitudes, infused together with DJ moves and something that became known as Turntableism."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Explosion of Flavors in the 90s
podcast.body: As the 90s progressed, the number of artists under the Alternative Dance umbrella "exploded," leading to "a million flavors" such as Post disco, electrical clash, new rave, and big beat. "As the 90s progressed, the number of artists that fell under the umbrella of Alternative Dance exploded. A million flavors appeared."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-Punk Subgenre
podcast.body: Alternative dance music emerged from Technopop, forming part of the diverse subgenres that arose during the post-punk era. "and a form of alternative dance"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
